evidence.claim: US passport holders may enter Andorra visa-free for stays up to 90 days; Andorra itself imposes no visa, but entry is only possible by first crossing into Spain or France (Schengen members)
Schengen entry (which governs the physical Andorra crossing via Spain/France) requires a passport valid at least 3 months beyond the planned departure date and issued within the last 10 years

US State Department travel advisory level for Andorra could not be freshly fetched this pass — travel.state.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches (Cloudflare-gated, resolves only via an interactive browser tool). Secondary sources widely report Level 1 (Exercise Normal Precautions), but this is not independently confirmed against the primary source, so the guide's advisory field is left unset rather than shipped unverified.
Andorra uses the euro despite not being an EU member, via a bilateral monetary agreement that also lets it mint its own coins
Catalan is Andorra's sole official language; Spanish is the most widely spoken second language, with French and Portuguese also common
Emergency numbers: 112 general, 110 police, 116 medical, 118 fire/mountain rescue; main hospital is Nostra Senyora de Meritxell in Escaldes-Engordany
The EHIC is not valid in Andorra; Andorra has reciprocal healthcare agreements only with Spain, France and Portugal, not the US — uninsured visitors are billed directly for care
Andorra's general IGI sales tax rate is 4.5%, with reduced rates of 0%/1%/2.5% and an increased 9.5% rate for specific categories

Direct Bus runs Barcelona airport (T1/T2) ↔ Andorra la Vella roughly every 2 hours, first departure 07:30/07:45, last 23:00/23:15 outbound and 06:15–22:15 return, ≈3.5-hour journey, fares from €31.50–35 one-way
Direct Bus operates 365 days a year on this route; only 24/25/31 Dec and 1 Jan schedules may vary
Nov–Apr: Casa de la Vall is open Tuesday–Saturday 10:00–14:00 and 15:00–18:00; closed Sundays and Mondays
General admission €5, reduced €2.50 (groups 10+, seniors 65+, foreign students); guided tour +€1.50/person with advance reservation
11th–12th century Romanesque church holding the largest Romanesque apse in Andorra, remodelled 1940 by Josep Puig i Cadafalch; free entry, not wheelchair accessible
Barri Antic is Andorra la Vella's historic quarter, centred on Carrer Major/Carrer de la Vall/Carrer del Pui, holding Casa de la Vall and Sant Esteve church
Mercat de la Vall runs first Saturday of the month, May–October 2026 (with an August extension to Sunday Aug 2); does not operate in November
Visiting only the Roc del Quer mirador (without the Tibetan bridge) is exclusively by private car via the Montaup road; no bus service reaches the viewpoint alone
Official guidance recommends doing routes above 1,700 m only between end-of-June and end-of-September for safety

No direct bus reaches the Engolasters lakeside trailhead; access is by car/taxi to the Ctra. d'Engolasters road or on foot from the Escaldes-Engordany tourist office
Caldea is a large thermal spa in Escaldes-Engordany (thermal lagoons, saunas, Indo-Roman baths), a short walk/bus ride from central Andorra la Vella

Borda Estevet, Ctra. de la Comella i de la Plana 2, Andorra la Vella; open 13:00–16:00 and 20:00–23:00; reservation via phone/WhatsApp (+376 864026); mountain/Mediterranean cuisine, capacity 250

Casa de la Vall (Andorra's historic 16th-century parliament house, Barri Antic) is open Nov–Apr 10:00–14:00 & 15:00–18:00, closed Sundays and Mondays; admission is by reservation only via +376 839760 or museusandorra@gmail.com — no walk-up visits. Standard admission €5, concessions €2.50.

Church of Santa Coloma (Andorra la Vella's oldest church, 8th–9th c. nave with a unique 12th-c. circular Lombard bell tower) is open Jan–May & Oct–Dec 10:00–14:00 & 15:00–18:00, closed Sun/Mon; €7 standard admission. Unlike Casa de la Vall, self-guided audioguide visits do NOT require advance reservation — only the guided-tour option does (book via +376 839760 / reservesmuseus@govern.ad).

MiraKbé gastrobar (Carrer Pere d'Urg 10, Andorra la Vella) runs a weekday lunch set-menu Mon–Fri 13:00–15:15 (€12, incl. water/wine/beer) and an à la carte tapas dinner service; phone/floor service runs 10:00–16:00 & 19:00–23:00 Mon–Sat, closed Sundays.

MiraKbé is recommended over Andorra la Vella's touristy main shopping street by an independent food blog and a separate diner account, both citing better value and quality away from the busier tourist strip.

Borda Estevet (traditional Andorran mountain-grill restaurant, Andorra la Vella) takes bookings via its own online form, phone (+376 864 026), or WhatsApp; lunch service runs 13:00–16:00, dinner 20:00–23:00. No deposit, cancellation, or walk-in policy is stated on the page itself.

The official Llac d'Engolasters hiking route is 1.9 km, +350/-45 m elevation, rated Easy, roughly a 2-hour round trip (1h15 out, 45 min back) — a good fit for moderate walkers on a first Pyrenees trip without a full mountain-day commitment.
The Roc del Quer viewpoint / Tibetan bridge (operated by Pont Tibetà Canillo) posts hours of 9:30–19:00 daily (Mon–Fri and Sat–Sun alike), with no seasonal closure stated on the operator's own page.
Andorra's official tourism board describes Roc del Quer as remaining open year-round, Monday to Sunday, paid access, 'weather permitting' — i.e. no fixed seasonal closing date.

Catalan is Andorra's sole official language (Constitution of 1993). 2022 survey data: Catalan is the habitual language for 63.7% of the population, Spanish for 48.6%, Portuguese 6.6%, French 5.7% (respondents can name more than one) — Spanish, Portuguese and French usage stems mainly from Spanish/Portuguese immigration and from French/Spanish tourism; only Catalan is native to Andorra.

The EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) became fully operational on 10 April 2026 across all Schengen external border-crossing points, including land borders. It applies to non-EU short-stay visitors (e.g. US passport holders) and captures facial image, fingerprints, and travel-document data. This is a live, active change from the pre-2026 baseline a generic guide would assume for crossing into Andorra.

Direct Bus's Barcelona–El Prat Airport → Andorra la Vella coach runs 7 daily departures per terminal (T1: 07:30, 11:00, 13:00, 15:00, 17:30, 20:00, 23:00; T2: +15 min each), arriving in Andorra after approximately 3h30; passengers should arrive 30 min before departure; service runs 365 days/year.

transport.route: Barcelona–El Prat Airport (T1/T2) ↔ Andorra la Vella, Direct Bus coach
transport.doorToDoor: ≈3.5 hours airport to the Andorra la Vella bus station, plus a 5–10 minute walk into the Barri Antic
transport.transferReality: No transfer — one direct coach, no interchange required. Andorra is outside the Schengen area, so this trip's Schengen entry happens at the Barcelona/Girona/Toulouse airport, not at the Andorra–Spain/France land crossing. As of 10 April 2026 the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) is fully operational and captures a facial image + fingerprints from non-EU short-stay visitors at that airport crossing — a real change from the pre-2026 baseline a generic guide would assume.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: Standard coach luggage hold; unremarkable for two travelers with normal luggage
transport.buffer: Arrive 30 minutes before departure; build in extra slack in November for possible mountain-road weather delays, and extra time at the airport end for EES biometric processing on this trip's first Schengen entry
transport.missedConnection: Next departure is roughly 2-3.5 hours later on a normal day (7 scheduled departures per terminal); missing the last practical pre-flight return bus likely means an expensive, unverified-cost taxi (≈3+ hours) or a missed flight — there is no rail alternative
transport.nextService: Seven scheduled departures a day per terminal (T1: 07:30, 11:00, 13:00, 15:00, 17:30, 20:00, 23:00; T2: +15 min each); return 06:15–22:15
transport.lastPracticalReturn: For a same-day flight, work backward from departure time using the full ≈3.5-hour ride plus a real buffer — the scheduled last bus (22:15) leaves far too little margin for most flights
transport.fallback: Andbus (Novatel) runs a parallel Barcelona-airport shuttle; taxi is the fallback of last resort — no train or Andorra-based airport exists

disagreements.topic: Whether the Llac d'Engolasters / Engolasters-area trails are a reasonable pick for an early-November visit
disagreements.investigation: A generic aggregator/blog source suggested November is a good, quiet time to walk the Engolasters loop. Fetched three separate official visitandorra.com trail pages directly (Circuit de les Fonts, the Engolasters short-distance route, and the Llac d'Engolasters route itself); all three consistently name June–September (or May–October at best) as the recommended hiking season, and the wider Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley page explicitly flags routes above 1,700 m as unsafe outside that window.
disagreements.resolution: Trusted the official trail authority over the aggregator lead. Shipped Llac d'Engolasters (1,616 m, below the 1,700 m safety line) as the trip's nature pick since it clears the altitude threshold, but hedged the day plan with an explicit winter-conditions caveat and a Caldea plan_b on a rain/snow trigger, rather than presenting the hike as an unconditional good idea for these dates.

disagreements.topic: Whether short-stay tourists (non-resident, non-EU passport) crossing the Andorra–Spain/France land border are covered by Andorra's EU border-management carve-out, or remain subject to full EES registration like any other Schengen external-border crossing
disagreements.investigation: The EU Commission's own EES page (fetched) states the system applies broadly to non-EU short-stay visitors at all Schengen external border-crossing points, land borders included, with no Andorra-specific carve-out mentioned. Andorran press (Alto.ad — fetched; digitalandorra.com, elperiodic.ad, laciutat.cat — search-preview, Catalan-language) describes a Govern d'Andorra–EU Border Management Agreement, but its exemption from EES registration is explicitly scoped to third-country nationals holding Andorran residency permits, not short-stay tourists; the same coverage separately reports Andorra secured 'random' rather than 'systematic' vehicle checks at the land border to avoid a traffic collapse.
disagreements.resolution: Bounded rather than fully closed: since EES applies broadly to non-EU short-stay visitors at Schengen external borders and this party's FIRST such crossing is the Barcelona/Girona/Toulouse airport (not the Andorra land border), the guide treats the airport leg as the definite EES touchpoint and builds a buffer note there. The Andorra-side land-crossing nuance (resident-only carve-out vs. random-vs-systematic vehicle checks) doesn't change which candidates ship or the day plan, only a logistics buffer note, so it's recorded here rather than investigated further this pass; govern.ad's own EES guidance page should be re-checked closer to the trip (its nav-only fetch this pass returned no substantive text).

disagreements.topic: Whether Roc del Quer viewpoint / Tibetan bridge might close in November for weather/safety reasons
disagreements.investigation: The viewpoint's own operator page (ponttibetacanillo.com, fetched) and the official visitandorra.com page (fetched) both describe it as open on a regular daily schedule 'weather permitting' with no stated seasonal closure window. A third-party travel blog (estiber.com, fetched) instead states the site 'puede cerrarse en invierno por motivos de seguridad' (may close in winter for safety reasons), without citing a specific date range.
disagreements.resolution: Moot for this guide regardless of how it resolves: Roc del Quer stays rejected on the separate, unambiguous car-only-access constraint (no bus reaches the mirador), so the seasonal-closure question doesn't change which candidates ship. Folded into the 'what generic guides get wrong' divergence item as supporting detail (it's open, but unreachable without a car) rather than left as an open question.

saturation.note: Andorra la Vella is a small single-city, single-parish-adjacent destination. Across both independent passes and the three ranked priorities, 19 distinct candidates were evaluated (5 culture/history, 8 food/dining, 6 nature/outdoors, after deduping candidates both passes independently reached). Later searches in both passes kept surfacing the same handful of aggregator-listed names with no new official-tier sources behind them. Reconciliation resolved every conflict the two passes produced: MiraKbé flipped from Pass A's thin-sourcing rejection to shipped once Pass B climbed to its official site; Roc del Quer stayed rejected on car-only access despite Pass B shipping it under a differently-named candidate id, since neither pass found a bus route to the mirador; Caldea stayed shipped per Pass A despite Pass B's priority-fit caution, since it remains the trip's only verified wet-weather contingency for the nature/outdoors day. The two remaining open threads (the EES land-border carve-out nuance; Roc del Quer's unconfirmed winter-closure blog claim) are bounded disagreements that affect a buffer note and a rejected candidate's supporting detail respectively, not which candidates ship or the day plan's structure.
